data.title: Senators warn GENIUS Act rules could push stablecoin firms toward federal oversight
data.description:
Six bipartisan senators on Tuesday urged the US Treasury Department to extend proposed regulatory protections to state-supervised stablecoin issuers, warning that proposed GENIUS Act rules could steer firms toward federal licenses.

In a letter to Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, Senators Cynthia Lummis and Kirsten Gillibrand, along with Angela Alsobrooks, Kevin Cramer, Pete Ricketts and Mark Warner, said Treasury’s proposal offers a safe harbor to certain issuers with pending federal applications and regulator-approved waivers, but no equivalent protection for state issuers.

The senators warned that issuers “may be incentivized to seek greater operational clarity under a federal license,” including through the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC), which they said was “the opposite of our intent in drafting this legislation.”

The senators urged Treasury to extend the safe harbor to issuers in states expected to have qualifying frameworks in place before Jan. 18, 2028, reducing uncertainty while certification reviews are pending.

The senators’ request follows a June appeal, urging Treasury to preserve state participation and clarify the certification process.

The GENIUS Act generally allows issuers with $10 billion or less in outstanding stablecoins to operate under qualifying state supervision, with exemptions available above that threshold.

Kevin Wysocki, head of policy at Anchorage Digital, questioned whether a broader safe harbor would make much difference. He said issuers are choosing federal oversight because they risk having to switch regulators if their stablecoins exceed $10 billion in circulation, although exemptions are available.

data.title: Copper price hits 7-month low: Voltas, PG Electroplast, Blue Star shares rally up to 7% on input cost relief hopes
data.description:
Shares of air-conditioning and cooling products manufacturers witnessed significant rally in today’s trading session, November 19, as copper prices tumbled to their lowest level in seven months, raising expectations of lower input costs and improved margin prospects for companies engaged in the sector.

On Wednesday, copper prices slipped to 7-month-low as a stronger US dollar, growing concerns over Chinese industrial demand and a selloff in AI-related stocks overshadowed tightening supplies of the metal.

Three-month copper futures on the London Metal Exchange fell 4.6 percent to $12,471.00 a metric ton, the lowest settlement since April 7. Front month copper fell 5.3 percent in New York to $5.6595 a pound, also the lowest since April 7, reported WSJ.

AC stocks buz in today’s trade on likely input cost benefits

Stocks such as Voltas, Blue Star, PG Electroplast and Amber Enterprises India rallied up to 6 percent during the session, on optimism over the potential benefits of easing raw material costs.

Voltas and PG Electroplast were leading the gains. Shares of Voltas rallied opened at Rs 1,133.20 and rallied 6.6 percent to touch an intra-day high of Rs 1,207.45 from its previous close of Rs 1,132.10. At around 10.47 am, the stock was trading 6.8 percent higher at Rs 1204.35, on the BSE.

Shares of PG Electroplast opened at Rs 539.15 and climbed as much as 6 percent to an intra-day high of Rs 570.75 from its previous closing of Rs 538.25. At around 10.47 am, the stock was trading 5,42 percent higher at Rs 567.40, on the BSE.

Shares of Blue Star opened at Rs 1,620 and surged 5.5 percent to hit an intra-day high of Rs 1,708 compared with the previous closing of Rs 1,618.30.

Shares of Crompton Greaves Consumer Electricals opened at Rs 208.85 and gained 4.7 percent to touch an intra-day high of Rs 216.75 from the previous closing of Rs 207.

Meanwhile, shares of Amber Enterprises India Ltd opened at Rs 6,253.90 and rallied 3.6 percent to hit an intra-day high of Rs 6,451, compared with the previous closing price of Rs 6,222.20.

data.title: Malaysia's Stronger 3Q Growth Unlikely to Prompt Bank Negara Rate Hike — Market Talk
data.description: Malaysia's stronger-than-expected 3Q GDP growth is unlikely to materially raise the probability of a Bank Negara Malaysia rate increase in January 2027, CIMB economists Chew Khai Yen and Michelle Chia say in a note. Private consumption growth has moderated, while uneven services activity and easing services inflation point to limited demand-driven price pressures, they say. BNM is likely to remain focused on the inflation outlook, particularly amid upside risks from higher production costs, weather disruptions as well as coming income and wage measures, they reckon. CIMB expects 4Q GDP growth to moderate to 5.1% from 5.5% in 3Q. It raises Malaysia's 2026 growth forecast to 5.5% from 5.0%, but maintains its view that the policy rate will stay at 2.75% in January. (yingxian.wong@wsj.com)

data.title: Lenovo Slips To Loss In Q2, Despite Higher AI-related Revenues; Sees Long-term Growth; Shares Drop
data.description:
BEIJING (dpa-AFX) - Shares of Lenovo Group Ltd. (LNVGY.PK, 0992.HK) were losing around 3 percent in Hong Kong trading after the Chinese PC and mobile maker reported Thursday a loss in its second quarter of fiscal 2027, compared to prior year's profit, hurt mainly by surge in operating expenses. Revenues, however, climbed from last year, mainly driven by growth in AI-related revenue.

Looking ahead, Lenovo said it aims to capture long-term demand for AI compute and deliver sustainable, profitable growth.

In the second quarter, net loss attributable to equity holders was $640 million or 5.17 cents per share, compared to prior year's profit of $340 million or 2.52 cents per share.

Adjusted attributable net profit was $1.361 billion, compared to $512 million last year.

Operating loss was $117 million, compared to prior year's operating profit of $643 million, reflecting 98 percent year-over-year surge in operating expenses to $4.96 billion.

Group revenue, however, climbed 48 percent to an all-time high of $30.24 billion from last year's $20.45 billion.

All business groups delivered record second-fiscal-quarter revenue while demonstrating strong profitability. The Infrastructure Solutions Group became an engine of hyper-growth with operating profit surpassing $1 billion for the first time, the firm noted.

AI-related revenue grew 79 percent year-on-year, surpassing the $10 billion mark for the first time and accounting for 36 percent of total Group revenue in the quarter.

Cloud Service Provider revenue for the Group grew nearly 170 percent year-on-year, and Enterprise & SMB infrastructure revenue was up 200 percent year-on-year.

Further, Lenovo's Board of Directors declared an interim dividend of 9.0 HK cents per share.

Looking ahead, Lenovo said it remains highly confident in the long-term growth opportunities across both infrastructure and devices. As AI shifts from training to inferencing, rapidly expanding real-world use cases are driving sustained compute demand across cloud, edge, and enterprise environments, the firm added.

In Hong Kong, Lenovo shares were trading at HK$16.720, down 2.79 percent.

data.title: Loading ... Claude and GTA VI
data.description:
A look at the day ahead in European and global markets from Ankur Banerjee

The latest test of how investors feel about the AI trade is here as Claude chatbot maker Anthropic gets ready for its market debut after clinching an eye-watering $1.5 trillion valuation in the biggest-ever initial public offering.

Anthropic is the first major frontier AI model developer to go public and priced its IPO at $83 apiece, raising $81 billion to claim the title of the largest stock-market debut on record.

Investors say demand is robust for the offering, suggesting a strong opening day, though Asian equities are not basking in the afterglow. Worries about AI profitability and the massive debt-fuelled spending to build related infrastructure have dented sentiment for weeks and Thursday was no different in Asia.

US stock futures, though, pointed higher on the IPO pricing while European stocks were set for a strong opening, suggesting Asia's place as the epicentre of the AI boom has meant it is also feeling the pain much more.

Taiwan's stock market is where most of the action is this week, with the benchmark index TWSE:TAIEX down 3.4%, on pace for a weekly decline of 11%. South Korea's KOSPI was flat, set for a 4% weekly fall.

Hawkish comments from the Federal Reserve also cast a shadow over Asian markets, with traders bracing for a hike next month. Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said if the central bank wanted to get inflation down, it needed to take more "aggressive action." Traders are pricing in a 10% chance of a 50-basis-point hike, the CME FedWatch tool showed.

That left the dollar standing tall at an 18-month high against major rivals. The yen remains perilously close to the 160-per-dollar mark, leaving traders jittery about intervention. The Asian currency is down 1.8% so far in 2026 as authorities in Tokyo stepped in to support the yen in several bouts of intervention earlier this year.

Anthropic's debut is not the only eagerly awaited event on Thursday, with "Grand Theft Auto VI" rolling out across the globe after 13 years and an estimated $1 billion or more in production costs. Early reviews for the game, which could bring in billions of dollars for its developer, Take-Two Interactive studio Rockstar Games, are euphoric.

Key developments that could influence markets on Thursday:

Anthropic market debut, Walmart earnings, GTA VI debut

data.title: Australian Dollar Slides as Thoughts Turn to RBA Rate Cuts
data.description:
By James Glynn

SYDNEY--The Australian dollar weakened after news the country's unemployment in October surged to its highest level since 2021.

The Aussie fell to around 66.60 U.S. cents after the data was released early Thursday, hitting its weakest levels since January, from around 67.20 U.S. cents just prior.

Economists were surprised by a rise in unemployment to 4.9% in October from 4.7% in September, which brought with it a fall in employment of close to 50,000 jobs over the month.

The data immediately cast doubt on whether the Reserve Bank of Australia would be able to raise interest rates further, after delivering five increases since the start of the year.

To be sure, the discussion in financial markets also turned more fully to the question of when the RBA might start cutting interest rates.

Interest rate swap markets had been pricing a 28% chance of an interest rate rise by February. After the data, that shifted to a 20% chance of an interest rate cut by March.

An interest rate cut by November next year is now fully priced in.

Taylor Nugent, an economist at National Australia Bank, said unemployment is already well above where the RBA had expected it to be in the final months of the year, which supports the case that the interest rate tightening cycle is over.

NAB expects the RBA will start cutting interest rates in August next year as the economy slows and inflation pressures ease.

Currency traders are weighing competing influences as it was only on Tuesday that RBA Governor Michele Bullock reaffirmed her view that inflation risks remain skewed to the upside.

Bullock said the problem with inflation is that it isn't just due to high oil prices, adding that domestic price pressures are also strong, fueled in part by a boom in data center investment.

Also, wages in the third quarter grew at their fastest pace in three years, something that will further stoke fears at the RBA that high inflation expectations are becoming embedded.

Inflation data for October will also be published next week with economists fearing that it could bring more bad news for the RBA.

The central bank recently forecast that inflation won't return to the target of 2.5% until mid-2028, leaving it open to a lot of forecast error.

Still, traders are now more comfortable about ruling out a further interest rate rise by the RBA.

"The weaker-than-expected jobs data reinforces our view, and market expectations, that the RBA's tightening cycle is over and its next move will be a rate cut," said Carol Kong, currency strategist at the Commonwealth Bank of Australia.

CBA is now forecasting two interest rate cuts in August and November, she added.

"The dovish repricing of RBA policy has pushed Australian dollar back to where it started the year. We continue to see the path of least resistance for the currency as lower over the coming months," Kong added.

  • Write to James Glynn at james.glynn@wsj.com

data.title: Bharat Forge invests in India subsidiary KSSL
data.description:
Indian manufacturer Bharat Forge (BSE: 500493) has invested INR2.905bn ($31.08mn) in its wholly owned subsidiary Kalyani Strategic Systems Limited (KSSL) through a rights issue, the company said in a stock exchange filing on November 18.

The capital comes from money that Bharat Forge raised in an earlier Qualified Institutional Placement and had set aside for this purpose. The company's board of directors approved the additional investment in KSSL at a meeting on November 5. In return, Bharat Forge received 290.508mn fully paid-up equity shares in KSSL.

Each share has a face value of INR10 and was issued at par. The shares were allotted on November 18, according to the filing. The company made the disclosure under Regulation 30 of the Securities and Exchange Board of India's rules on listing obligations and disclosure requirements. Bharat Forge said it had already published the details required under those rules, and under a SEBI master circular dated January 30, 2026, when it announced the board's approval on November 5.

Company Secretary and Compliance Officer Tejaswini Chaudhari signed the filing, which was sent to the Bombay Stock Exchange and the National Stock Exchange of India. Bharat Forge is based in Mundhwa, Pune, in the western Indian state of Maharashtra.

data.title: PB Fintech shares fall up to 6% after co-founder Alok Bansal to step down from executive role next year
data.description:
Shares of PB Fintech Ltd. declined up to 6% on Thursday, November 19, as the the company's co-founder, executive vice-chairman Alok Bansal has decided to step down from his executive role. The stock has since recovered most of its losses.

PB Fintech, in an exchange filing on Wednesday, said Bansal's last day as executive vice-chairman and whole-time director and as key managerial personnel / senior management will be March 31, 2027.

Bansal will continue on the company's board as a non-executive, non-independent director from April 1, 2027, the company said.

The board of directors on Wednesday approved the change in designation, on the recommendation of the Nomination and Remuneration Committee. The same is subject to the approval of shareholders of the company.

Alok Bansal has stated the change is on account of his personal desire to step back from day-to-day executive responsibilities, according to the regulatory filing. He has confirmed there is no other material reason for the change.

The board placed on record its appreciation for Bansal's significance and contributions to the company over the past 18 years and his role in building and strengthening its businesses and leadership team, PB Fintech said.

The stock has since recovered from the lows of the day, and is now trading 2.1% lower at ₹1,014.3. Its intraday low of ₹970.4 was below its IPO price of ₹980.

data.title: The Iran War Could Permanently Slash Reliance on Hormuz, IEA Says
data.description:
By Giulia Petroni

Shipping disruptions due to the Iran war have shattered confidence in the Strait of Hormuz, spurring a costly overhaul of the global energy trade that could dramatically cut the world's dependence on the route over the next decade, the International Energy Agency said.

Before the conflict, around 20 million barrels of oil a day passed through Hormuz, a narrow waterway connecting the Persian Gulf to global markets. That could fall to 8.5 million barrels a day by 2030 and to less than 2 million by 2035 if the strait remains severely disrupted, the Paris-based agency said in its World Energy Outlook.

"The Hormuz crisis has delivered a huge shock to the system," IEA Executive Director Fatih Birol said. "I don't see any credible pathway for the energy world to return to the way it was before."

Still, the Middle East is set to remain the world's largest exporter of oil to international markets as major Gulf producers race to build alternative pipelines and routes.

Since the Iran war began in late February, Saudi Arabia has relied on its East-West pipeline to move crude toward the Red Sea, while the United Arab Emirates used its pipeline to the port of Fujairah on the Gulf of Oman.

Now, around 7 million barrels a day of new pipeline capacity is under construction or under consideration to help Gulf producers move oil without passing through the strait, the IEA said. Building the projects will require an estimated $40 billion of investment, adding about $2 to the cost of each barrel of Middle Eastern oil exported, the agency estimates.

"It is not easy, but the energy world could conceivably manage without the strait," Birol said. "It cannot manage without the Middle East."

Meanwhile, global oil prices have been volatile: Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, swung from around $71 a barrel prewar to peaks above $126, before falling back toward $93 a barrel in November.

The price reaction was less severe than the scale of the disruption might have suggested, coinciding with a time of ample global supply and well-stocked inventories.

The IEA now expects the global oil market to swing back into oversupply as Middle Eastern production recovers faster than global demand growth. From a surplus of 1.7 million barrels a day in the current quarter, the glut is set to widen further next year to about 3.8 million barrels a day.

Between March and October, global oil demand fell by around 3.7 million barrels a day from a year earlier, as higher prices, physical shortages, government-imposed measures and weaker economic activity curbed consumption.

The decline was particularly sharp in the Middle East, where demand dropped 10%, and Asia, where it fell 5%. China's seaborne crude imports fell to around 6 million barrels a day in June from 11.6 million in February as the country drew down inventories, restricted fuel exports and switched between fuels.

Over time, the IEA also expects the crisis to reinforce a broader shift toward countries' domestic energy sources. Renewables and nuclear energy will be the biggest beneficiaries, while energy-efficiency measures, biofuels and, in some Asian countries, coal could also gain ground.

"All in all, countries want to rely more and more on homegrown energy," Birol said.

Volatile fuel prices have reinforced the case for electrification. Global demand for electricity has grown faster than the world economy since 2019 and at twice the rate of overall energy demand, driven by electric vehicles, air conditioning, industrial motors, heat pumps and data centers. The IEA expects electricity demand to accelerate further through 2035, with electricity approaching 30% of final energy consumption across all scenarios.

In its World Energy Outlook, the IEA presents a series of possible scenarios rather than a single forecast.

data.title: Japan's Meiko boosts Vietnam PCB plant investment to $800mn
data.description:
Japanese printed circuit board (PCB) manufacturer Meiko Electronics (6787) has added $450mn to its factory project in northern Vietnam, raising total investment in the plant to $800mn.

According to The Investor, Meiko (6787), which started establishing itself in Vietnam close to two decades ago, is expanding that footprint with the larger budget, a move that coincides with rising global demand for sophisticated circuit boards found in high-end mobile phones, satellite communications equipment and servers for artificial intelligence.

Construction began in June on the factory, which subsidiary Meiko Hoa Binh Electronics operates in Phu Tho province's Bo Trai Song Da Industrial Park. Under the updated plan, the building will rise to five storeys instead of three, and its floor space will double from 60,000 sqm to 120,000 square metres.

The extra funds will lift yearly output in the second phase to 261,000 sqm, up from 180,000 sqm. Designed capacity will total 504,000 sqm per year once the site runs at full scale, which Meiko expects by the end of its 2026 fiscal year on March 31, 2027.

The factory makes high-frequency, high-density substrate-like PCBs and high density interconnect (HDI) boards. It started volume output of AI server boards in August 2026 and runs dedicated lines for a large US smartphone client. Meiko also plans to mass-produce optical transceiver components, which carry very fast data traffic inside AI data centres and cloud networks.

The company is spending more at its other Vietnamese sites as well. Planned capital expenditure at its fourth plant in Hanoi rose to JPY45bn ($282.25mn) from JPY25bn. The plant builds high-layer-count HDI boards for satellite and AI uses, along with memory module substrates. Spending at the Quang Minh plant in Hanoi increased to JPY50bn from JPY40bn.

Spending on the Yen Quang facility, also located in Phu Tho, is being doubled to JPY120bn from the previous JPY60bn, and the site's floor area will expand to 200,000 sqm. Its main customer base will be the satellite communications sector. Quang Minh and Yen Quang are both expected to be running at full scale during the latter half of fiscal 2027.

Meiko set up Meiko Electronics Vietnam in Hanoi in 2006. It opened an electronics assembly plant in 2008 and began making PCBs in 2010. Today it has more than 6,000 staff in the country.

In the fiscal year to March 31, 2026, Meiko Electronics Vietnam posted net sales of JPY113.64bn, an increase of 25.7% on the previous year. Net profit grew 32% to JPY9.71bn.

data.title: Musk: Jensen Huang irreplaceable, regrets midterm spend
data.description:
Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk likened Jensen Huang’s departure from Nvidia to kicking Michael Jordan off a team riding a winning streak, while expressing regret over how much he spent on the U.S. midterm elections.

“You’ve got a winning streak ... and then you kick Michael Jordan off your team,” Musk told during an interview at The New York Times’ DealBook Summit on Wednesday. He added, “Doesn’t seem like a smart decision to me.”

The SpaceX and Tesla chief executive, who previously said it would be an “honor” to hire the Nvidia co-founder, added that no one could really replace Huang. Musk said he had heard similar views about Huang’s departure from Nvidia, including from President Donald Trump.

“I think the president has voiced publicly that he thinks Jensen should have stayed as CEO, and everyone I know thinks the same ... this is, at the end of the day, the Nvidia board decision,” he said, adding, “We’re not on the board, right?”

Tesla has been one of Nvidia’s key customers, while Huang has frequently commended Musk’s AI ambitions, particularly Tesla’s autonomous driving technology, xAI, and its Optimus humanoid robot.

Asked about the midterms, Musk said he felt “pretty foolish” about spending at least $474M with little to show for it, though he added that “maybe it would have been much worse without that,” according to a CNBC report.

Musk said his goal had been to prevent the presidency, House, and Senate from all being controlled by one party. “If I could rewind the clock, I would have spent less money,” he added.

data.title: Why Did DIS, TGT, ASO Stocks Surge To 52-Week Highs Today?
data.description:
Key points:
  • Disney stock reached a 52-week high of $123.37 after Q4 revenue rose 16% to $25.9 billion.
  • Target stock hit a two-year high of $171.91 after its Q3 results beat Street expectations.
  • Academy Sports gained as its fiscal 2026 expansion is set to reach 23 new locations across 10 states. 

Walt Disney Co. (DIS), Target Corp. (TGT) and Academy Sports and Outdoors (ASO) stocks climbed to fresh 52-week highs on Wednesday as strong earnings, improving shopper traffic and ambitious store expansion fueled investor optimism.

Disney and Target stocks gained 4% each, while Academy Sports stock climbed 5%.

Disney’s Growth Makes Analysts Raise Price Targets

Walt Disney stock hit an annual high of $123.37 after the entertainment giant reported stronger-than-expected fiscal fourth-quarter (Q4) results across its Entertainment, Experiences and Sports businesses. Revenue climbed 16% year-on-year to $25.9 billion, while operating income increased 43% to $5 billion. Adjusted earnings reached $1.77 per share, beating analysts’ consensus estimate of $1.68.

The results evoked positive reactions from Wall Street, with Needham increasing its price target to $135 from $125 and Raymond James lifting its target to $133 from $119. Both firms maintained bullish ratings on the stock. Analysts also pointed to Disney's planned $3 billion in cost savings through fiscal 2029.

Disney+ and Hulu helped drive growth in the Entertainment division, which brought in $11.9 billion in revenue. Its Experiences business’s revenue was $10.1 billion, supported by more visitors to U.S. theme parks and higher customer spending.

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around the stock remained ‘extremely bullish’.

Target Benefits From Higher Store Traffic 

Target stock reached over a two-year high of $171.91 after the retailer exceeded Q3 Wall Street estimates and raised its full-year outlook. Revenue rose 7.1% to $27.1 billion. Adjusted earnings came in at $2.65 per share, compared with the $2.08 analyst consensus.

However, Target's earnings included a $0.50-per-share boost from tariff refunds. Without that benefit, adjusted EPS was $2.15. Comparable sales grew 5.6%, helped by a 5% rise in store traffic. The company now expects 2026 sales to grow about 6% and guided annual EPS to $10.65 to $11.40.

Retail sentiment around the stock improved to ‘extremely bullish’ from ‘bullish’.

Academy Sports Advances Its Store Expansion Plan

Academy Sports stock also climbed to a two-year high of $73.82 as the sporting goods retailer moved closer to completing its fiscal 2026 expansion program. The company is adding locations in regional markets as it looks to boost its physical retail presence.

Academy opened two new stores in Marshall and Magnolia, Texas, and plans to open another in Pascagoula, Mississippi, before the fiscal year ends. This will bring its 2026 total to 23 new stores across 10 states. Retail sentiment toward the stock remained ‘bullish’.

So far this year, DIS, TGT and ASO stocks have gained between 7% and 69%.

data.title: Hong Kong stocks hit 4-month low, as US-China tensions weigh on tech
data.description:
Hong Kong's benchmark stock index sank nearly 2% to hit four-month lows while China shares sagged further, as fresh trade tensions flared up between the US and China despite symbolic meetings between Xi Jinping and Donald Trump in the Chinese tech hub of Shenzhen.

** Risk appetite is also curbed by the prospect of further US rate hikes that will likely tighten global liquidity.

** Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index was down 1.9% by the lunch break, plumbing the lowest level since late June. The Hang Seng Tech Index hit a 26-month low.

** In China, both the blue-chip CSI300 Index and the Shanghai Composite Index fell roughly 0.4%, touching the lowest in more than a year.

** Investors worry that the world's two largest economies are careening toward a fresh tit-for-tat trade war spiral, after Republicans' defeat in the US midterm election appears to have prompted the White House to take a more hawkish policy against China.

** The Nvidia saga has already led to tighter controls over advanced chip exports and other measures to slow China's progress in AI.

** Sources told Reuters that the Trump administration is considering requiring US companies to publicly disclose their use of Chinese AI models in a bid to discourage reliance on the technology. Meanwhile, a US House panel asked Microsoft on Wednesday to brief lawmakers on a report which said the company could allow the Chinese firm ByteDance to use OpenAI models through Microsoft's Azure cloud platform.

** Hong Kong-listed AI model developers and AI hyperscalers, whose competitiveness depends on advanced computing power, tumbled on Thursday.

** Minimax slumped 8% to record lows while Z.AI tumbled 6%.

** Tencent dropped nearly 7% to more than two-year lows after its third-quarter revenue missed forecasts, and the company said new US chip curbs may slow model training.

** In China, tech stocks in areas that rely on advanced chips, including cloud computing (.CSI931469), artificial intelligence and big data , led the declines.

data.title: Indian shares edge higher despite Asia selloff; IT caps gains
data.description:
By Bharath Rajeswaran and Vivek Kumar M

Indian shares defied a selloff in Asian markets on Thursday, led by auto and financial stocks, although weakness in IT shares, following hawkish signals from the Federal Reserve, capped gains.

The Nifty 50 rose 0.20% to 25,280.05 and the Sensex gained 0.19% to 82,194.23 as of 10:38 a.m. IST.

MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan (.MISX00000PUS) fell about 1.9%, as continued selling in AI-linked stocks and hawkish signals from the Fed weighed on sentiment.

While the Nifty faced "profit-taking in the previous session, the broader bullish structure remains intact," said Sudeep Shah, head of technical and derivatives research at SBI Securities.

"On the upside, 25,370-25,400 remains the immediate hurdle and a sustained breakout above this zone could signal a resumption of the uptrend towards 25,600."

Thirteen of 16 major sectors advanced, while the broader small-cap and mid-cap indexes added about 0.1% and 0.4%, respectively.

The auto index climbed 3.3%, supported by resilient vehicle demand after the festive season and lower crude and metal prices, which eased input cost pressures.

Banks gained 0.6% and state-owned lenders rose 2%, extending a November rally underpinned by foreign buying, steady earnings and attractive valuations.

Financials, oil and gas, and auto stocks have risen 10%-18.5% this month, helping drive the benchmark indexes about 10% higher.

Meanwhile, minutes from the Fed's October meeting showed that policymakers saw a need to intensify efforts to curb inflation, though they agreed to hold interest rates steady for now.

IT stocks fell 2.1% as the prospect of higher US rates renewed concerns about client technology spending, according to analysts. Indian IT companies derive a significant share of revenue from the United States.

Among stocks, online-payment firms Paytm , One Mobikwik and Pine Labs fell 6%, 6.7% and 4.3%, respectively, following reports of a potential delay in the government's rollout of the merchant discount rate.

data.title: Piramal Pharma to acquire remaining 26% stake in Yapan Bio
data.description:
Piramal Pharma Limited said it would acquire the remaining 26 per cent equity stake in Yapan Bio Private Limited, a subsidiary of the company, from its existing shareholders.

The administrative committee authorised by Piramal Pharma’s board of directors has “approved the exercise of the company’s call option to acquire the balance 26 per cent equity stake in Yapan Bio Private Limited,” the drugmaker said in an announcement to the stock exchange.

Acquisition terms yet to be finalised

The final terms of the acquisition, including the acquisition consideration and the effective date of transfer of shares, are yet to be finalised, it added.

“Consequent to the exercise of the call option, the company is engaged in discussions with the shareholders of Yapan in relation to matters necessary for consummation of the proposed transaction,” it said.

Yapan to become a wholly owned subsidiary

Yapan is a contract development and manufacturing organisation focused on services for vaccines and biologics. After the proposed transaction is completed, Piramal Pharma’s shareholding in Yapan is expected to increase from the present 74 per cent to 100 per cent, making it a wholly owned subsidiary, it said.
